*Topics — What a work is about. **Loss landscapes** — the geometry of trained solutions in weight space — mode connectivity, linear and along curves, barriers between minima and the permutation symmetries that hide or remove them, re-basin alignment, star domains and connecting simplexes, local versus global landscape structure, and model merging as its use (ADR-027).

| [THEORY-105](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-105.md) v2 | Fine-tuned hull points beat their own members | Gueta et al. (2023), [LIT-658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-658.md): RoBERTa-base models fine-tuned on the same dataset, the same task family, or any of 12 GLUE and SuperGLUE datasets cluster in weight space. Sampled points in the convex hull of each group beat the group's own members in 88% to 96.7% of comparisons. Extrapolating past the members raises the loss quickly, so the members sit near the region's edge and averaging moves inward. The paper calls the region convex, but shows only that the hull lies inside it, by a probe-based loss. Its reading of model soups and SWA as picking points inside the region is argued in its §8, not tested. Moving from the centroid towards the origin stays low-loss far past the members, which the authors cannot explain. Promoted 2026-10-20 on the probe-loss comparisons measured (ADR-047 v3); the geometric thesis is THEORY-828. | Active |
| [THEORY-107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-107.md) | Merging loses accuracy through interference | Yadav et al. (2023), [LIT-675](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-675.md): keeping only the top 20% of each task vector by magnitude loses almost nothing, so most of an update is redundant. Among the entries that remain, signs conflict between models, more so as more models are merged. Merging (IA)³ models with the multitask model's signs reaches 72.0 against 73.1 for multitask training and 66.4 for TIES with elected signs. That is the strongest evidence that sign is the bottleneck. But the oracle signs come from training on every task's data, the ablation finds rescaling and the disjoint mean matter more than election, and conflicts are as frequent among checkpoints of one task as across tasks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-108](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-108.md) | Connectivity, not flatness, predicts accuracy | Yang, Hodgkinson, Theisen, Zou, Gonzalez, Ramchandran & Mahoney (2021), [LIT-663](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-663.md): thousands of trained networks on a load by temperature grid, measured by the endpoint Hessian, by mode connectivity on a trained Bezier curve between two independent runs, and by CKA of their outputs. | [THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md) v4 | Linear connectivity implies feature linearity | Zhou et al. (2023), [LIT-674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-674.md): whenever two image classifiers are linearly mode connected, by spawning or by permutation, the features of nearly every layer of the interpolated network are proportional to the interpolation of the endpoints' features. This is layerwise linear feature connectivity, and two conditions, weak additivity of ReLU and a commutativity of weights with features, imply it exactly. Lubana et al.'s Lemma 2, [LIT-669](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-669.md), gives the exact one-hidden-layer case: linear connectivity between interpolating minima forces shared activation patterns, and with shared patterns the hidden features are linear along the path. Measured on pairs at three interpolation points, image classification only. The regularity outside image classification, and the step to many-model averages such as soups and SWA, are QUESTION-318. | Active |

Merging only the early layers and keeping later layers as task heads recovers most of the ensemble's accuracy. | [THEORY-116](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-116.md) v2 | Surviving barriers mark different mechanisms | Lubana et al. (2022), [LIT-669](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-669.md): models that rely on a synthetic cue and models that ignore it are separated by a linear barrier even after permutation matching. Fine-tuned models that keep a linear path to their parent keep its cue, and those that lose the path lose the cue. Their Conjecture 1 states this claim's direction. What their Appendix F.3 proves, for a one-hidden-layer ReLU network with interpolating minima, is the converse: linear connectivity forces identical activation patterns, so models relying on attributes of different complexity cannot be linearly connected under any permutation. Zhou et al. (2023), [LIT-674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-674.md), support that converse in deep image classifiers, where linearly connected pairs have features that blend layer by layer. The stated direction rests on experiments with synthetic cues and on a one-layer sufficiency argument. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-184](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-184.md) v2 | Equivariant updates keep coincident neurons | Yang, Poggio, Chuang and Ziyin (2025), [LIT-861](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-861.md), read in [NOTE-663](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-663.md). If an update commutes with permuting neurons (GD, SGD or Adam on a permutation-symmetric loss) and its map is K-Lipschitz, one step of size η changes every pairwise neuron distance by a factor in [1 − ηK, 1 + ηK]. This is a proved constraint on trajectories. It does not say that training simplifies above 1/K, that neurons never merge in the limit, or that any scale-dependent shape of the neuron cloud is preserved. | Active |
| [THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md) v2 | Converged SGD samples a modified Gibbs law | Kunin et al. (2021), [LIT-1011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1011.md), read in [NOTE-711](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-711.md). Modelled as an underdamped Langevin equation with noise covariance proportional to the Hessian, SGD at the end of training converges to a nonequilibrium stationary state: Gibbs on a modified loss whose curvature undoes the Hessian's anisotropy, with inverse temperature S(1 − β²), in broken detailed balance. A ResNet-18 on ImageNet explores isotropically in a plane where the loss is anisotropic, oscillates at Hessian-dependent rates, and moves at the predicted speed across a hyperparameter sweep. For the learned-structure line, a trained solution is in part a property of the regime that trained it. Proposed: the deep-learning evidence is one network, under assumptions the paper concedes are strained. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-210](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-210.md) v2 | Init and optimizer set position on symmetry orbits | Zhao, Walters & Yu (2025), [LIT-970](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-970.md), read in [NOTE-712](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-712.md): a survey, so the dynamical results are secondhand. Continuous parameter-space symmetries (GL, scaling, orthogonal, translation) make minima positive-dimensional and connected, which is one source of mode connectivity. Under gradient flow each gives a conserved quantity, such as layer imbalance, that is fixed by initialization and locates the endpoint on the manifold. Under SGD these are not conserved. Read first-hand (Neural Mechanics; Ziyin et al.), weight decay drives the conserved quantities toward zero, and minibatch noise drives a rescaling symmetry's toward the point where the layers' gradient noise balances. The survey had reported this as imbalance decaying with large learning rates, and a stationary distribution biased toward balanced solutions that a Langevin model does not predict. This is the null-space half that [THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md)'s limiting dynamics leave out. Proposed: one survey, with the SGD results unread here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md) v5 | SGD noise equalizes noise across symmetric groups | Ziyin, Li & Ueda ([LIT-1012](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1012.md), read in [NOTE-714](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-714.md)), with the gradient flow conservation law and the Itô term from Neural Mechanics ([LIT-1013](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1013.md)). If ℓ(u, w) = ℓ(λu, w/λ) for every sample, then under the SDE model of SGD d(‖u‖² − ‖w‖²)/dt = −T(uᵀC₁u − wᵀC₂w), with T = η/S. The noise has no component along the symmetry, but its dependence on the parameters produces a deterministic drift through Itô's lemma. The drift points to the noise-balanced point, and weight decay adds to its rate. In a diagonal linear network the stationary distribution follows exactly: it is non-ergodic, has a memory of initialization, and collapses to zero above a critical temperature. The law is re-derived here (2026-10-19) within the SDE model; the tests are small synthetic networks, and whether it holds in deep networks on real data is QUESTION-164. | Active |
| [THEORY-213](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-213.md) v4 | Weight decay puts minima on mirror subspaces | Ziyin (2024), [LIT-1014](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1014.md), read in [NOTE-716](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-716.md). If a per-sample loss is invariant under the reflection I − 2OOᵀ, then Oᵀθ = 0 is a stationary condition for GD and SGD. The Hessian is block diagonal there. Above a critical weight decay all minima satisfy the constraint. Under SGD with strong noise the subspace is attractive even at a strict saddle, by a Lyapunov-exponent argument. Rescaling, rotation and permutation symmetries imply mirrors, so they yield sparsity, low rank and merged neurons, with collapse and loss of plasticity as consequences. The SGD half is approximate and the network evidence is limited; the title holds only the exact half. Promoted on 2026-10-20 on the exact half, re-derived. The SGD half is QUESTION-206. | Active |
| [THEORY-278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-278.md) v5 | MSE training follows a central path to collapse | Han, Papyan & Donoho (2021), [LIT-974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-974.md), read in [NOTE-783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-783.md). MSE loss splits exactly into a least-squares term and a non-negative deviation term, and the deviation becomes negligible early in training in 15 dataset–network cells. On that central path, with λ = 0, the loss is ½ Σ 1/(ω_j² + C) in the singular values of Σ_W^(−1/2)M̃. Under a flow that re-whitens the features after every step, each ω_j grows as (4t/N)^(1/4), and their ratios tend to 1. That is NC1 and NC2, and NC3–NC4 follow. Not shown: that ordinary training is this flow, or anything for cross-entropy or with weight decay. | Active |
| [THEORY-286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-286.md) v2 | Imbalance yields SELI, not simplex ETF | Thrampoulidis et al. (2022), [LIT-994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-994.md), read in [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md). For the unconstrained-features max-margin problem under STEP imbalance, every solution has logits ŴᵀĤ = Ẑ (one-hot minus 1/k), ĤᵀĤ = UΛUᵀ and ŴᵀŴ = VΛVᵀ from Ẑ's SVD (Theorem 1). This is the ETF only if the data are balanced or binary. No finite ridge gives it under imbalance (Proposition 1), though the ridge path tends to it (Proposition 2). ResNet-18 and VGG-13 runs sit closer to SELI than to the ETF, and approach it more slowly at larger R. Not shown: that gradient descent reaches it, and anything with more than one seed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-425](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-425.md) v3 | Clean-data mode paths shed backdoors | Zhao, Chen, Das, Ramamurthy & Lin (2020), [LIT-668](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-668.md), read in [NOTE-530](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-530.md). A quadratic Bezier path trained on 50–2,500 clean samples between two backdoored VGG-16s on CIFAR-10 has, at t = 0.1, 88% clean accuracy and 1.1% backdoor success with 2,500 samples, and 63% and 2.5% with 50; injected weight errors fail at every point of such paths. | [THEORY-509](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-509.md) | MoE gate symmetry is only expert permutation | Tran, Trinh, Bui & Nguyen (2025), [LIT-670](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-670.md), read in [NOTE-513](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-513.md). Softmax is invariant to a common shift of scores and the sum to the order of terms, so G(n) = ℝ^d × ℝ × S_n preserves the layer; Theorems 4.1–4.2 show that generically it is all of the gate's symmetry, for dense gating and for top-k with k ≥ 2 (top-1 has an extra scaling). Aligning expert order and then each expert's hidden units gives barriers of 0.0044–0.0066 between GPT-2 MoE layers fine-tuned from different seeds, against 0.14–0.86 without the order step. Every experiment shares and freezes the backbone around the inserted layer, so it is not evidence about independently trained MoE models. | Active |
| [THEORY-521](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-521.md) | Generalization error can jump at critical load | Martin & Mahoney (2017), [LIT-672](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-672.md), read in [NOTE-542](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-542.md), restating Seung, Sompolinsky & Tishby (1992) and Haussler, Kearns, Seung & Tishby (1996), which the record does not hold. Generalization is set by maximizing s(ε) − α ln(1/(1 − ε)). For weights on a sphere s(ε) ~ ln ε and ε ~ 1/α; for ±1 weights s(ε) ~ −(π²/2)ε² ln ε, the first-order condition has no solution past a critical load, and the error drops to zero. Uniform bounds that see a class only through its size or VC dimension are smooth and blind to this. That deep networks have such a phase diagram is the authors' conjecture, and their mapping of label noise to load and early stopping to temperature is an analogy. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-732](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-732.md) v2 | Layerwise linearity explains mode connectivity | Zhou et al. (2023), [LIT-674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-674.md), read in [NOTE-512](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-512.md) with Appendix A's proofs checked: for an L-layer ReLU MLP on a finite dataset, weak additivity of ReLU over the two networks' pre-activations and the commutativity W_A H_B + W_B H_A = W_A H_A + W_B H_B at every layer make the interpolated network's features at every layer exactly the interpolation of the endpoints' features (Theorem 1). | [THEORY-736](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-736.md) v2 | Dropout-stable solutions are mode connected | Kuditipudi et al. (2019), [LIT-671](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-671.md), Theorem 1, read in full in [NOTE-544](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-544.md), with Draxler et al.'s (2018) concatenation bound from [LIT-653](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-653.md). Dropout stability gives every solution a half-width copy with the same loss up to ε. Half the units are then free, so working units can be swapped in and permuted at no cost. That joins any two such solutions. It is a statement about dropout-stable solutions only: whether training produces them is [THEORY-109](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-109.md)'s open question, and Theorem 4 of the same paper builds disconnected global minima. | Active |
| [THEORY-741](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-741.md) | Wide nets' global minima share a linked minimum | Lin, Li and Wu (2024), [LIT-682](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-682.md), Theorems 6, 11 and 18 with Lemmas 7 and 25, read in [NOTE-535](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-535.md) and re-derived by the promotion audit. Two toy models whose minima can be written down: a two-layer ReLU student of an orthonormal teacher on the sphere at population loss, and a deep linear network fitting y = Qx. Spare width lets every minimum be moved, along segments of minima, to one a common centre can reach. No permutation symmetry is used, and nothing is claimed about trained networks. | Active |

The authors present the law as general to networks with rescaling symmetry, but test it only on small synthetic networks. This THEORY holds the general claim, for deep networks on real data, which no measurement in the record yet supports. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-797](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-797.md) v2 | MSE nets reach collapse along the central path | Han, Papyan & Donoho (2021; ICLR 2022), [LIT-974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-974.md), read in [NOTE-783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-783.md). Renormalization is imposed, not measured, and every experiment used weight decay, which the derivation excludes. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-1272](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1272.md) | Late SGD weights drift sub-diffusively | Hennick and De Baerdemacker (2025; ICLR 2026), [LIT-1879](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1879.md), read in [NOTE-1467](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1467.md). Late-training displacement fits R(t) ∝ t^α with α below ½ on MNIST MLPs, TinyStories models and ImageNet convnets fine-tuned with SGD, read through the Alexander–Orbach relation as α = d_s/(2λ) with d_s ≤ λ. Proposed: d_s is obtained by fitting that same relation, so the fits test the power law and not its link to the LLC; Kunin et al. report super-diffusion in another regime. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1275.md) v2 | SGD transitions only partly match the posterior | Chen, Lau, Mendel, Wei and Murfet (2023), [LIT-1894](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1894.md), read in [NOTE-1462](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1462.md). Their Bayesian antecedent hypothesis is one-way: training's transitions have Bayesian counterparts. From their numbers the antecedents of the chain 4⁺⁺⁻ → 4⁺ → 5 → 5⁺ fall at n ≈ 190, 370 and 1,600–2,500, rising with training. But the posterior's transition 5 → 6 at n ≈ 600 was not seen in training, and SGD on 1000 samples ends at the 5-gon, a 4-gon variant or the 5⁺-gon, none of which the posterior at n = 1000 favours; it favours the 6-gon. The rising order holds at the point estimates, not across the estimates' spread. One model, one SGD setting, estimated learning coefficients; the computation was re-run by a second checker on 2026-11-06 (scratch/formal/tms_critical_sizes_check.py). | Active |
| [THEORY-1872](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1872.md) | Low-frequency update gaps hurt merging | Zheng & Wang (2025), [LIT-2643](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2643.md), read in [NOTE-1974](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1974.md). Amplitude variance across tasks is largest at low index-grid frequencies and correlates negatively with normalized merged accuracy; FR-Merging (high-pass then magnitude-weighted sum) reaches 78.1 on ViT-B/32 with 8 tasks against 70.1 for task arithmetic and 73.6 for TIES. The frequencies are over the arbitrary order of rows and columns and change under a function-preserving permutation of hidden units, which the paper does not test. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1874](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1874.md) | Orthogonalising low-rank updates aids merging | Gargiulo et al. (2025), [LIT-2627](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2627.md), read in [NOTE-1990](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1990.md). Keeping 3% of each task's singular components per layer costs 1.5% accuracy; cross-task singular-vector overlap is highest in early layers; TSV-M reaches 85.86 against 70.79 for task arithmetic on ViT-B/32 with 8 tasks; the ablation needs both truncation and decorrelation. That overlap is the cause rests on an association over three task sets. A rival diagnosis to TIES's sign conflicts, [THEORY-107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-107.md). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1879](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1879.md) | Low-variance LoRA projections reduce merge loss | Zhang & Zhou (2025), [LIT-2650](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2650.md), read in [NOTE-1965](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1965.md). The term is B2A2h1, task 2's update on task 1's input; OSRM minimizes ‖A_t H_¬tᵀ‖_F over orthonormal A_t, whose solution is the r smallest-eigenvalue eigenvectors of the other tasks' feature covariance. On Llama3-8B it lifts task arithmetic from 63.28 to 72.75 but leaves TIES at 52.69 against 53.01, and its gains shrink with model size. That the output shift is the cause is the paper's account; it does not measure the term falling with the gain. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1890](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1890.md) | Fine-tunes from one start interpolate features | Zhou, Chen, Chen, Zhang & Yan (2024), [LIT-2646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2646.md), read in [NOTE-1973](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1973.md). Cross-task linearity: cosine near 1 and projection-length ratio near 1 between the interpolated model's features and the interpolated features, against an endpoint baseline, in the blocks reported; the same for soups of 5 CIFAR-10 and 10 ImageNet ViT-B/32 fine-tunes, all blocks for the latter. Extends [THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md) from proportionality to approximate equality and from pairs connected in loss to pairs that are not. Bears on both halves of [QUESTION-318](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-318.md) and supports [CLAIM-498](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-498.md)'s averaging step for soups, not SWA. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1892](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1892.md) | Task arithmetic rests on weight disentanglement | Ortiz-Jimenez, Favero & Frossard (2023), [LIT-2634](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2634.md), read in [NOTE-1979](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1979.md). Post-hoc linearised CLIP models lose single-task accuracy, so ordinary fine-tuning is nonlinear; disentanglement error is small near the pretrained weights; linearised fine-tuning raises task addition by up to 5.8 points and negation forgetting by up to 13.1, less for larger models; from random initialisation task addition is near chance. Disentanglement is by construction equivalent to the property it explains. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1897](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1897.md) v2 | Merge non-additivity is mostly carried transport | Zhu (2026), [LIT-2629](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2629.md), read in [NOTE-1989](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1989.md) (v1 in full to §8, v3 skimmed). On Qwen2.5-1.5B, with reduced replications on Llama-3.2-1B and Qwen2.5-7B: about 65–70% of the cross-term's layerwise flux is transport, with gain 1.08–1.14 per late block; erased at depth 3 or 8 it returns at ρ ≈ 1.00/0.99; erased along its own direction it removes about 19% of expressed interference, and norm-matched wrong directions make interference worse. v3, retitled, finds the same term a bystander where merging collapses, so its effect is on output non-additivity, not on whether the merge works. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1898](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1898.md) | Shared directions inflate merged singular values | Li et al. (2026), [LIT-2655](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2655.md), read in [NOTE-1964](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1964.md). A projection analysis under plain addition (Lemma 3.2, Theorem 3.3) shows positive cross-task overlap inflating merged singular values, with the largest overlaps in the top subspaces. Singular Value Calibration lifts task arithmetic from 68.9 to 81.9 on ViT-B/32 with 8 tasks, above TIES's 72.6 in the same runs, and improves TIES, DARE and TSV-M, the last by under a point. A rival diagnosis to sign conflict, [THEORY-107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-107.md). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1901](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1901.md) | Domain fine-tunes share more singular subspace | Chaves et al. (2026), [LIT-2636](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2636.md), read in [NOTE-1994](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1994.md). Pairwise SAR is 0.61–0.71 among DomainNet domains and 0.41–0.69 among eight vision tasks (Fig. 2). SCORE averages 65.69 on ViT-B-32 against 64.95 for TSV and 64.84 for TIES, and 73.04 on ViT-L-14 against 72.46 for TIES (Table 1), with no seeds reported. The paper reads the overlap as the cause of conflict; that link is argued, not tested. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1903](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1903.md) | Rescaling mean so(d) generator lifts OFT merges | Yang, Shi & Liu (2026), [LIT-2645](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2645.md), read in [NOTE-1993](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1993.md). Each task's rotation is mapped to so(d) by the inverse Cayley transform (not a matrix logarithm), the generators are averaged, the mean is rescaled by Σ‖Q_i‖/‖ΣQ_i‖, and the result is mapped back by the Cayley transform. The ablation separates the geometry from the rescaling: averaging in so(d) without it scores 41.01, barely above averaging rotations directly (39.53). One base model, the authors' own experts, no seeds. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1904](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1904.md) | Task vectors add and negate task skills | Ilharco et al. (2023), [LIT-2638](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2638.md), read in [NOTE-1970](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1970.md). Negation of a CLIP ViT-L/14 task vector cut target accuracy by 45.8 points with little change on ImageNet; adding eight image tasks' vectors reached 91.2% normalized accuracy; GPT-2 toxicity and T5 GLUE follow. All within one pretrained start, with λ tuned per edit on validation data. The paper offers no mechanism: that near-orthogonal task vectors enable addition is its speculation. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1905](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1905.md) | Routed LoRA concatenation keeps subject fidelity | Wei et al. (2026), [LIT-2626](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2626.md), read in [NOTE-1978](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1978.md). The router R = QG⁻¹ is the least-squares solution of the layer-local reconstruction objective (Theorem 3.1) and is absorbed into B, so the merged model is one static LoRA; task arithmetic is R = I. At K = 9 on FLUX.1-dev it scores DINO 0.6713 against 0.4723 for TIES and 0.6240 for IterIS, a 90.2% recovery. One LoRA pool, no seeds. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1996](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1996.md) | LoRA merge non-additivity depends on inputs | Zhu, Li and Cai (2026), [LIT-2779](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2779.md), read in [NOTE-2078](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2078.md). At Qwen2.5-1.5B the matched contrast code+safety minus code+math is about +6.0 on code prompts and +0.1 on math prompts; it persists at 0.5B, 7B, under full fine-tuning at 0.5B and in Llama-3.1-8B. On the same code prompts the Alpaca template the adapters were trained on collapses it from +6.9 to +0.3, and an untrained ChatML template leaves it at +12.5. The companion, Zhu (2026), [LIT-2629](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2629.md), traces the collapse to a denominator effect in the readout. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-2157](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2157.md) | LLC estimator is only calibrated in linear nets | Lau, Furman, Wang, Murfet and Wei, [LIT-2995](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2995.md), read in [NOTE-2239](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2239.md). The estimator behind the record's learning-coefficient entries ([THEORY-1275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1275.md), [THEORY-975](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-975.md)). The estimate is a free-energy slope at effective sample size n/log n, cut off also by the localizer's γ; the paper fixes β*, sets γ per experiment, and calibrates only in noiseless deep linear networks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2160](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2160.md) | LLC plateaus divide training into stages | Hoogland, Wang, Farrugia-Roberts, Carroll, Wei and Murfet, [LIT-2966](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2966.md), read in [NOTE-2248](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2248.md). Stages of transformer training read off pauses in the local learning coefficient, matched to behavioural and structural changes. Motivated by Bayesian singular learning, not derived from it; the coefficient's decreases are unexplained; the estimator is run at one fixed nβ and γ per setting. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2161](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2161.md) | SGD's top-Hessian component doesn't train | Song, Ahn and Yun, [LIT-2973](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2973.md), read in [NOTE-2250](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2250.md). Gradient alignment with the dominant Hessian subspace is not where training happens: the loss falls along a steep valley's flat floor, in the complement of the top k. A weak instance of a model's rankings of directions disagreeing ([CLAIM-835](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-835.md)), within one metric. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2163](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2163.md) | Fisher singularities cause learning plateaus | Amari, Park and Ozeki (2006), [LIT-2960](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2960.md), read in [NOTE-2255](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2255.md). Where network singularities are and what they do to learning: critical sets at finite parameters, cone apices in the space of distributions, a Milnor attractor for gradient flow, a slow manifold that makes the plateau, and repulsion under natural gradient. With the truth at the singularity, the gradient along the degenerate direction is cubic (Eq. 5.13), so the approach is algebraic, u ∝ t^(−1/2) (the reader's derivation; the paper states no rate). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2164](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2164.md) | Overlap singularities are Milnor-like attractors | Wei, Zhang, Cousseau, Ozeki and Amari (2008), [LIT-3000](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3000.md), read in [NOTE-2254](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2254.md). Orbits, not time courses: a conserved quantity of the averaged flow fixes where learning goes near coinciding units, and the long plateau on the singularity is a noise-driven walk along a line of equivalent models, not a slow decay along a degenerate direction. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2171](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2171.md) | Teacher spike detaches by a BBP transition | Park and colleagues, [LIT-2990](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2990.md), read in [NOTE-2260](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2260.md). A dynamical reading of the BBP transition: the outlier's appearance in the weight spectrum is a matter of step size and time, while the signal is in the weights from the first step. Its UTKFace experiments find the leading first-layer directions tracking the data's principal components only in the large-step regime. Grounds [CLAIM-799](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-799.md) ([ARG-171](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-171.md)) and the rival reading [CLAIM-855](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-855.md) ([ARG-174](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-174.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2191](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2191.md) | Bayesian influence flips sign during training | Lee, Smith, Adam & Hoogland (2025), [LIT-3001](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3001.md), read in [NOTE-2279](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2279.md). Influence as a susceptibility that changes at stage transitions. The sharp edges: the theory is for a Bayesian posterior split between two phases, and the link to SGD is the paper's "primary theoretical gap"; peaks are predicted only "under some conditions"; in the toy, the order of the peaks is the order of the modes' strengths. A.2 names the "Type-B" transition, equal loss with a falling LLC, without testing it. Proposed until reproduced. | Proposed |
